claims.text: The release-version column in the IaC tool comparison table reflects the latest stable releases as of 2026-09-21, and the version and release-date figures were checked against each project's GitHub releases on 2026-09-21.
In the at-a-glance table, the latest stable release of Pulumi (as of 2026-09-21) is v3.261.0, released 2026-09-02.
In the at-a-glance table, the latest stable release of Terraform (as of 2026-09-21) is v1.16.1, released 2026-09-02.
In the at-a-glance table, the latest stable release of AWS CDK (as of 2026-09-21) is v2.268.0, released 2026-09-02.
The latest stable release of Pulumi is v3.263.0, released 2026-09-16.
The latest stable release of Terraform is v1.16.3, released 2026-09-16.
The latest stable release of AWS CDK is v2.270.0, released 2026-09-17.
The latest stable release of Azure Bicep is v0.47.16, released 2026-09-08.
The latest stable release of Kubernetes is v1.37.0, released 2026-08-26.
The latest stable release of Crossplane is v2.4.1, released 2026-09-15.
The latest stable release of OpenTofu as of 2026-09-21 is v1.12.6, released 2026-08-19.
Pulumi, AWS CDK, Kubernetes, and Crossplane are licensed under Apache-2.0; Azure Bicep is licensed under MIT; OpenTofu is licensed under MPL-2.0.
Terraform is licensed under BUSL-1.1, which is not OSI-approved, and is governed by HashiCorp, an IBM company.
Pulumi is governed by Pulumi Corporation, Kubernetes and Crossplane are governed by the CNCF, and OpenTofu is governed by the Linux Foundation.
The pricing tables reflect published pricing as of September 2026.
Env zero is the current name of the company formerly known as env0.
Spacelift's paid plans scale by private worker count rather than by seats or resources, with quote-based pricing at the top end.
Env zero prices its paid tiers per successful apply or environment.
Spacelift and env zero are managed CI/CD layers frequently compared against the core IaC tools.
GitHub star counts as of 2026-09-21: Pulumi ~25.7k, Terraform ~49.7k, AWS CDK ~12.9k, Azure Bicep ~3.6k, Kubernetes ~127.9k, Crossplane ~12.1k, OpenTofu ~30.2k.

Among dedicated IaC tools, Terraform remains the most-starred on GitHub, followed by OpenTofu, Pulumi, AWS CDK, and Crossplane, and Kubernetes leads the broader infrastructure ecosystem by GitHub stars.
GitHub star counts for these tools were measured on 2026-09-21.

Terraform's larger community reflects a decade of first-mover adoption, while Pulumi, OpenTofu, and Crossplane have grown fastest among teams prioritizing general-purpose languages, open governance, or Kubernetes-native infrastructure management, respectively.
Kubernetes is the de facto container orchestration standard.
Google Cloud Deployment Manager reached end of support on March 31, 2026.

claims.text: Google Cloud Infrastructure Manager replaces Google Cloud Deployment Manager and automates deployment and management of Google Cloud resources using Terraform configurations.
Pulumi Cloud's Free edition is free forever for one user, with unlimited stacks and projects and 500 workflow minutes per month.
Pulumi Cloud's Essentials plan starts at $40/month, including 40 credits and up to 500 managed resources.
Pulumi Cloud's Pro plan starts at $400/month, including 400 credits and up to 2,000 managed resources.
Pulumi Cloud's Enterprise plan is custom, contract-priced.
HCP Terraform is free for up to 500 managed resources with one concurrent run, then moves to per-resource pricing of roughly $0.10 to $0.99 per resource per month depending on tier.
Self-hosted Terraform Enterprise is available at custom pricing for larger organizations.
The managed-platform pricing figures (Pulumi Cloud and HCP Terraform) reflect published pricing checked on 2026-09-21.
